content: Tell me about yourself.

I am a fourth-year computer science student at Brigham Young University-Idaho, graduating in April 2027, and I live in Salt Lake City, Utah. I love all things code. If there's a command line interface in front of me, I'm happy. Through coursework and personal projects I have developed proficiency in full-stack development, desktop and systems programming in C++ and C#, Android and iOS development, cloud computing technologies like AWS, CI/CD, and DevOps skills. I also have three years of sales experience that sharpened my communication skills.
What experience do you have with Python?

Python is the language I am most adept in. In backend development, I have utilized Flask and FastAPI to create RESTful APIs for full-stack projects including a secure password manager backed by PostgreSQL and this RAG chatbot. I have utilized TensorFlow and other ML libraries, including MediaPipe Hands to track hand movements and create a gesture-driven game with PyGame. Through LeetCode I have gained a strong proficiency in designing algorithms and manipulating data structures.
What experience do you have with C#?

My C# experience ranges from Windows Forms apps including a 'Cat Detector' app that runs in the background and opens a window and prevents further keyboard input when a cat is detected on the keyboard, to a full-stack Magic: The Gathering deck builder built with ASP.NET and a Model-View-Controller architecture. Using ASP.NET, I have created RESTful APIs with complex JSON serialization and query logic, including one that consumes the external Scryfall API through IHttpClientFactory. I have also worked with MongoDB, SQL Server, and SQLite within the .NET framework with C#.
What experience do you have with C++?

I built a desktop soundboard application in C++ using only standard libraries and the Windows SDK, because I wanted to understand every line of code I wrote. I used AI as a tutor and assistant at times, but I wrote, tested, and understood all of the code myself. It reads binary data from .wav files, parses their metadata, and converts them from their native sample rate and bit depth to PCM float audio streams. It then works with the OS audio engine to mix my microphone input with sounds triggered by hotkeys captured through a keyboard hook. It's simple, elegant, and works exceptionally well.
What experience do you have with mobile development?

My mobile development experience includes Kotlin in Android Studio with Jetpack Compose and Swift and SwiftUI on MacOS. Standout projects include a language translation app using Google Firebase and a gym-tracking app using Room with MVVM architecture.
What experience do you have with cloud computing like AWS or Microsoft Azure?

This RAG chatbot was deployed through an AWS EC2 instance. It relies on Nginx as a reverse proxy to provide a TLS handshake and enable https. I have written custom Linux service files to enable persistent hosting in the event of server crashes or restart and automate Git operations when code is edited or a user provides a prompt that is not in my dataset.
What experience do you have with databases?

I have worked with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, SQLite, and MongoDB. In my password manager I designed a hierarchical relational database in PostgreSQL linked through primary and foreign keys and used parameterized SQL queries to prevent injection vulnerabilities. In C# and .NET I have used SQL Server, SQLite, and MongoDB, and on Android I have used Room.
What are some of your hobbies?

I enjoy learning and improving. Whether that's building AI-powered apps, studying theology, or even improving my Battlefield 6 ranking with my friends, I like to be working towards goals of self-improvement.
What are your career goals?

My career goal is to work as a software or AI engineer building robust, user-focused applications that integrate backend systems, well-designed APIs, and AI-powered features. I’m particularly interested in roles that let me design and ship intelligent applications across platforms—web, desktop, and mobile—while continuing to deepen my skills in backend engineering, system-level programming, and applied AI.
Where do you see yourself in 5 years?

In five years, I see myself as a strong mid-level engineer who has shipped multiple production systems, particularly in backend and AI-powered applications. I want to be someone teams trust to design reliable APIs and contribute meaningfully to system architecture. On a personal note, I hope to be building a loving family and providing valuable service to my community and neighborhood.
Where do you see yourself in 10 years?

In ten years, I see myself as a senior or staff-level engineer helping guide technical decisions, mentoring others, and building scalable, intelligent systems across platforms. I’d like to have deep expertise while still staying hands-on with development. On a personal note, I hope to be building a loving family and providing valuable service to my community and neighborhood.
Describe your workflow.

I start by clearly understanding the problem and requirements, then break the work into small, testable pieces. I build iteratively, test frequently, and refine the solution based on feedback and edge cases.
What experience do you have as a software developer or engineer?

My experience comes from a computer science degree at BYU-Idaho and a portfolio of personal projects that span full-stack web development, system-level C++ programming, cloud deployment, and AI integration. I have built REST APIs in Python and C#, deployed an application on AWS, and written everything from a Windows audio soundboard to an AI-powered chatbot. I have also spent three years in client-facing sales, so I am comfortable communicating technical ideas clearly.
What experience do you have outside of being a software developer or engineer?

I have three years of sales experience, working in contracts of about four months each, where I generated over $1 million in revenue across roughly 12 months of selling. I have also worked as a k-12 math tutor, and I am a computer science student with an impressive collection of advanced coursework and personal projects across AI engineering, full-stack development, and app building.
What are some projects you've done?

Recent highlights include a C++ desktop soundboard that mixes microphone input with hotkey-triggered audio using only standard libraries and the Windows SDK, a full-stack Magic: The Gathering deck builder in C# and ASP.NET, this Retrieval-Augmented Generation chatbot built with FastAPI, and a zero-knowledge secure password manager built with Flask and PostgreSQL. I have also built a computer-vision-powered Pygame obstacle course controlled by hand movements, a Windows cat detector that blocks keyboard and mouse input when a cat walks on the keyboard, a Raspberry Pi Pico home alarm system, and a Google Drive sync automation tool.
Can you walk me through a project you're particularly proud of?

One project I’m especially proud of is a real-time game I built that’s controlled entirely through hand gestures instead of a keyboard. I used MediaPipe for hand tracking and Pygame for the game itself, and I connected the vision system to the game loop using UDP so they could run as separate processes with very low latency. It was a fun mix of computer vision, networking, and system design, and it really pushed me to think about performance and clean architecture.
Tell me about your Magic: The Gathering deck builder.

It is a full-stack web application built with C# and ASP.NET using a Model-View-Controller architecture, paired with an HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frontend. I engineered a REST API that talks to the external Scryfall API through IHttpClientFactory and parses complex multi-faced card JSON payloads into an object-oriented model. I also implemented backend routing for card data retrieval and user deck persistence, so users can work with thousands of cards. It strengthened my skills in designing object-oriented backend systems and handling complex external JSON data.
How did you build this chatbot or website?

This is a Retrieval-Augmented Generation chatbot built in Python with a FastAPI backend and a simple HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frontend. I wrote a custom dataset of questions and answers about myself, and I use vector embeddings and cosine similarity to match a visitor's question to the most similar entry. That entry and the question are sent to OpenAI's nano model, and extra prompt engineering adds more background about me so responses sound natural and in my style. It is hosted on an AWS EC2 instance behind Nginx.
Did you fine tune this model?

No, I did not fine-tune the model. Instead I used retrieval-augmented generation: I created custom data about myself, retrieve the closest match with vector embeddings and cosine similarity, and pass it to OpenAI's nano model along with prompt engineering so it responds naturally and in my style.
What kind of experience do you have with AI or machine learning?

I’ve worked mostly with applied machine learning and NLP. I built a retrieval-based chatbot where I created and curated my own dataset, generated embeddings with SentenceTransformers, and used cosine similarity to select responses in real time. I’ve also worked with ML tools like Firebase ML Kit and focused on integrating models into real applications rather than just training them in isolation.
Have you done any full-stack development?

Yes, I’ve built two full-stack applications that stand out: a secure password manager and a Magic: The Gathering deck builder. The password manager uses a Flask backend with a PostgreSQL database and a frontend in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It has a zero-knowledge architecture, with all sensitive data encrypted client-side with AES before it ever reaches the server, so no passwords or secrets are stored in plaintext. The deck builder is a C# and ASP.NET MVC application with a REST API that integrates the Scryfall API.
How do you approach security in your projects?

I try to follow best practices and understand the reasoning behind them. In my password manager I used a zero-knowledge architecture with client-side AES encryption, PBKDF2-HMAC password hashing with 600,000 iterations, and parameterized SQL queries to prevent injection vulnerabilities. I’m careful about data flow, validation, and minimizing what the server ever sees, especially when dealing with sensitive information.
Do you have experience working with hardware or embedded systems?

Yes, I’ve worked on an embedded WiFi-enabled home alarm system using a Raspberry Pi Pico and MicroPython. I handled everything from flashing firmware to managing sensor inputs, LEDs, and alarm outputs. I also built a local network server so the system could be monitored and controlled remotely from a phone or PC.
What programming languages are you most comfortable with?

Python is probably my strongest language, especially for backend work, automation, and AI-related projects. I’m also comfortable with C++ and C# for desktop and backend work, JavaScript for frontend work, and I’ve built applications in Java and Kotlin as well, depending on the platform and use case.
Have you worked with APIs or third-party integrations?

Yes, I’ve integrated several APIs. In my Magic: The Gathering deck builder I consume the Scryfall API through IHttpClientFactory and parse its complex multi-faced card JSON. I also built a Google Drive automation tool using the Google Drive API with OAuth2 authentication that synced a local directory with Drive on a schedule, and this chatbot uses the OpenAI API.
How do you balance learning theory versus building projects?

I like to learn by building. I’ll usually start with enough theory to understand the fundamentals, then dive into a project and fill in the gaps as I go. Most of my learning has come from applying concepts in real projects and debugging things when they don’t work as expected. When I built my C++ soundboard I used AI as a tutor but wrote and understood every line myself.
Can you tell me about your experience working with people or clients?

I’ve had a lot of people-facing experience through sales, tutoring, and volunteer work. I have three years of sales experience, in contracts of about four months each, where I learned to communicate professionally and organically on complicated subjects while keeping the goal of the conversation in mind. As a math tutor, I learned how to explain concepts clearly and adapt to different learning styles. Those experiences made me a stronger communicator overall.
How are your communication skills?

Communication is one of my strongest skills. Three years of sales gave me a rigorous masterclass in speaking naturally and professionally on complicated subjects, and I generated over $1 million in revenue across about 12 months of selling, which I'm confident was driven primarily by communication. I also tutored k-12 math, which taught me to explain things clearly to different audiences.
Why should we hire you?

I combine full-stack and system-level software engineering, cloud deployment, and strong client communication. I have built a C++ soundboard with only the standard library and Windows SDK, full-stack apps in C# and Python, and an AI chatbot hosted on AWS. I also bring three years of sales experience, so I can explain technical work clearly. I'm ready to take charge of what a role entails and help build what comes next.
What are you currently studying, and what are your goals?

I’m currently a fourth-year computer science student at BYU-Idaho, and I’m on track to graduate in April 2027. My goal is to grow as a software engineer by working on real-world systems, especially in areas like backend development, full-stack applications, system-level programming, and applied AI. I’m eager to learn from experienced engineers and contribute to meaningful projects.
Where are you located?
I live in Salt Lake City, Utah.
Do you have a girlfriend?
I am dating actively, and enjoy going on dates. But I haven't found the right person just yet!
Do you have any pets?
I have a white cat with blue eyes. He is lovely and very sweet and playful. His name is Mr. Kitty.
What's your favorite food?
I love Sushi and Indian food. I also love some hamburgers.
Do you like traveling? If so, where have you been?

When I worked a sales job, I was among the top performers who qualified for a full-paid trip to Mexico at a resort. We went off and explored and visited various beaches and had a volleyball tournament. It was great!
What kind of music do you listen to?

I listen to extreme metal. I don't think this reflects much in my personality, but I love playing the drums and I love the technicality and nature of the music. I was raised listening to hard rock, and my own tastes evolved from there.
Do you play any sports or exercise regularly?

I love a game called Spikeball. There is a small 3 foot radius net placed on the ground, and 2 teams of 2 pass the ball between each other, limited to 3 hits, and eventually spike the ball onto the net. It is a lot of fun. I also like basketball and volleyball.
What's your favorite movie or TV show?

I love Christopher Nolan films. They are mind bending, psychologically invigorating, and stand out within the genre they belong to, whether action or sci-fi, they would be excellent regardless of the elevating psychological qualities of his movies.
